caption:
OpenAI just hit back in Apple's trade secrets case.
In counterclaims filed November 27 in federal court in San Jose, OpenAI says Apple is "coercing and threatening" suppliers that build OpenAI's upcoming devices, and took OpenAI's own secrets.
Apple's original case goes to trial July 19, 2027.

Who do you think comes out of this fight ahead?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple on November 27, 2026, accusing the iPhone maker of taking OpenAI trade secrets and of keeping hardware suppliers away from OpenAI. The filing was first reported by the Financial Times, according to 9to5Mac and Stock Analysis, which also cited Reuters.

The claims were filed in federal court in San Jose, California, in the case Apple brought against OpenAI in July, according to Stock Analysis. That case, Apple Inc. v. Liu, is before Judge Edward Davila in the Northern District of California. Former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan, both named as defendants by Apple, joined the counterclaims.

The central new accusation concerns suppliers. According to the Financial Times reporting cited by 9to5Mac, OpenAI says Apple is coercing and threatening suppliers that work with OpenAI on its upcoming personal devices, and that Apple is trying to compete unfairly by any means available. Interesting Engineering reported that the filing also accuses Apple of using its size and wealth to hold back competition.

None of the reports name a specific supplier or describe a specific incident. Gadget Review noted that the coverage does not say which supplier relationships are at issue, and that the accusations have not been tested in court.

OpenAI also says Apple encouraged its own employees to keep corporate files in personal iCloud accounts and to handle company business over personal iMessage accounts, according to Stock Analysis and 9to5Mac. Interesting Engineering reported that the filing describes this practice as a trap for employees.
The counterclaims are trade secret theft under federal law, interference with contracts and unfair competition under California law, according to Stock Analysis.

Apple sued OpenAI, its hardware company io Products, Liu and Tan in July 2026, accusing them of taking confidential hardware information. Tan previously led product design for the iPhone and Apple Watch at Apple. OpenAI has characterized the case as an attempt to stop it from hiring Apple employees, 9to5Mac reported.

In an earlier filing in October, OpenAI said an employee who returned to Apple sent more than 100 confidential files about an unreleased OpenAI device to personal accounts. Apple said at the time that its search had found no OpenAI confidential information, according to Stock Analysis and 9to5Mac.

OpenAI is building its own personal devices and bought io, the hardware startup of former Apple design chief Jony Ive. Interesting Engineering put the price of that deal at $6.4 billion. Apple has asked the court for a preliminary injunction that would bar further use of what it calls its secrets before a verdict.

Apple had not publicly responded to the new allegations as of November 27, Interesting Engineering reported. Under the schedule Judge Davila set in October, Apple's case is scheduled to go to trial on July 19, 2027.

The countersuit turns a case about former employees into a fight over the supply chain. Apple and OpenAI would both need many of the same manufacturers and component makers for consumer devices, so a claim that Apple pressured those partners goes to the heart of whether OpenAI can ship hardware at all. The filing also gives OpenAI a way to put Apple's own security practices on trial alongside its people.
Watch whether Apple answers the supplier accusations in court and whether any supplier is identified in the filings ahead of the July 19, 2027 trial.
